Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: A high-throughput molecular dynamics study with a machine-learning method on predicting diffusion coefficient of hydrogen in α-iron grain boundaries
Paper_Metadata.Note: DOI not found in OCR text

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.1: Diffusion of hydrogen in bulk iron

Composition.Note: Pure BCC iron model system; hydrogen atoms used as probe, not a component of the material

Process_Text.original: The system is firstly heated from 333 K to 1000 K in 0.2 ns, then equilibrated at 1000 K for 0.5 ns, cooled from 1000 K to 333 K in 0.2 ns and equilibrated at 333 K for another 0.1 ns. The NPT ensemble is used with 0 pressure.
Process_Text.simplified: Annealing: 333 K → 1000 K (0.2 ns), hold at 1000 K (0.5 ns), 1000 K → 333 K (0.2 ns), hold at 333 K (0.1 ns); NPT ensemble, 0 pressure

Stage5_Diffusion_Simulation.Description: 10 hydrogen atoms randomly placed in box, energy minimization, followed by 10-ns equilibration in NVT ensemble at 333 K
Stage5_Diffusion_Simulation.Note: Also computed at 500 K, 666 K, and 999 K for validation against experimental data

Simulation_Metadata.Simulation_Text: Diffusion coefficients of hydrogen obtained via calculating MSD of hydrogen atom in iron with varied configurations; Eq.(1) D = lim(t→∞) (1/6N) Σ|r_i(t) - r_i(0)|²

Structure_Text.original: A pure BCC structure of iron is generated
Structure_Text.simplified: Single crystal BCC α-iron, no grain boundary

Properties.Note: Approximate value from text: 'In pure BCC iron, we find that the diffusion coefficient is about 7 × 10⁻⁵ cm²/s'; also computed at 500 K, 666 K, and 999 K (values only shown in Fig. 4, not reported in text)

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.2: Diffusion of hydrogen in grain boundaries

Composition.Note: Pure iron GB model system; 10 hydrogen atoms randomly placed as probe in diffusion process

Process_Text.original: In each sampling step, a pair of rotations are applied to the upper and the bottom grain, thus forming an interface with varied configurations and a gap of 0.1 nm. The constructed model is then sent to annealing and subsequent diffusion simulations.
Process_Text.simplified: Monte-Carlo sampling from SO(3) group to generate GB rotations; pair of rotations applied to upper and bottom grain with 0.1 nm gap; annealing then diffusion simulation

Stage1_GB_Construction.Rotation_Axis: Drawn from azimuthal angle (theta) and polar angle (phi) via spherical coordinates

Stage6_Diffusion_Simulation.Description: 10 hydrogen atoms randomly placed in box, energy minimization, followed by 10-ns equilibration in NVT ensemble at 333 K

Simulation_Metadata.BCC_Symmetry_Augmentation: Yes, data augmented according to BCC symmetry after collection
Simulation_Metadata.Simulation_Text: High-throughput MD with Monte-Carlo sampling from SO(3) group; rotation axis from theta (azimuthal) and phi (polar) angles; rotation angle randomized 0-360 deg; gap 0.1 nm between grains; BCC symmetry not considered in sampling but used for data augmentation

Structure_Text.original: Structural deviations from BCC iron lead to decrease in hydrogen diffusion. More BCC atoms lead to higher diffusion coefficient and vice versa. The disordered iron atoms are traps of hydrogen.
Structure_Text.simplified: Bicrystal GB models of α-iron with varied misorientation; non-BCC structured atoms at GB region act as hydrogen traps; percentage of non-BCC atoms ranges from ~10% (most common) to >40% (lowest diffusion)

Secondary_Phases.Phase_Name: Non-BCC disordered region at grain boundary
Secondary_Phases.Description: Atoms with non-BCC structure near grain boundaries; fraction ranges from ~10% (most common GB) to >40% (lowest diffusion GB)

GB_Diffusion_vs_Bulk_Lowest.Original_Values: about 0.1 % of the diffusion in the bulk
GB_Diffusion_vs_Bulk_Lowest.Description: Lowest diffusion rate with more than 40% of atoms being non-BCC structured

GB_Diffusion_vs_Bulk_Most_Common.Description: Most common diffusion coefficient in GB with about 10% atoms being non-BCC structured

GB_Diffusion_vs_Bulk_Overall.Original_Values: typically 1 % of that in the bulk BCC iron
GB_Diffusion_vs_Bulk_Overall.Description: The diffusion coefficient in GBs is typically 1% of that in the bulk BCC iron (stated in Conclusion)

Number_of_GB_Models_D_above_1e-5_cm2s.Description: 30 cases out of 512 with diffusion coefficient > 1×10⁻⁵ cm²/s

Number_of_GB_Models_D_above_7e-5_cm2s.Description: 2 cases with diffusion coefficient above 7×10⁻⁵ cm²/s

Properties.Note: Histogram of diffusion coefficients at 333 K collected from 512 GB structures; values below 1×10⁻⁵ cm²/s are the majority; specific individual GB values not reported in text except statistical descriptions (0.1% and 1% of bulk)
Diffusion of hydrogen within GBs is markedly reduced compared to that in bulk BCC iron, with a 99% decrease (from Abstract)

items.Sample_ID: Modified SchNet for H diffusion prediction
Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.3: Performance of the SchNet in predicting hydrogen diffusion coefficient

Composition.Note: ML model trained on 512 GB MD simulation results of α-iron; input: atomistic structural data; output: natural log of diffusion coefficient

Process_Text.original: The SchNet architecture is employed, with modifications on the embedding layer. Iron atoms are classified into 100 types based on binned RMSD from polyhedral template matching, then sent to embedding layer to obtain a 64-dimension vector. Loss function is MSE, optimizer is ADAM with 0.001 learning rate, batch size 32.
Process_Text.simplified: Modified SchNet: PTM-based RMSD binning (100 types, range 0-0.5), 64-dim embedding, MSE loss, ADAM optimizer (lr=0.001), batch size 32, 512 epochs

Simulation_Metadata.Embedding_Method: PTM RMSD binned into 100 types (range 0–0.5), producing 64-dimension embedding vector
Simulation_Metadata.Output: Natural log of hydrogen diffusion coefficient
Simulation_Metadata.Simulation_Text: Modified SchNet architecture: all atoms are iron so atom type embedding is replaced by PTM RMSD-based binning into 100 types; 64-dim embedding; summation pooling to yield system-level diffusion coefficient; trained on 512 MD samples (352 train, 128 validation, 32 test)

Structure_Text.original: Configurations of the modeled GBs correspond to the lowest, the most common and the highest diffusion coefficient of hydrogen are analyzed.
Structure_Text.simplified: ML model takes atomistic structure (positions + PTM RMSD types) as input to predict hydrogen diffusion coefficient

Properties.Property_Name: ML Model Training Loss (MSE, log scale)
ML Model Validation Loss (MSE, log scale)

Properties.Note: Most predictions are within 1 order of magnitude different to the MD results; single outlier about 2 orders of magnitude difference (occurs at about 1% chance)
